one_line: Agent-native shopping with human-governed purchase rules.
what_it_does: A storefront where an agent searches and builds carts while a server-side rules engine gates checkout, approvals, receipts, and undo.
leverage_rationale: WebMCP makes structured cart and checkout state available to an agent while preserving a human approval boundary; generic UI driving could approximate it but less reliably and with weaker governance.
leverage_evidence: About text describes eight native WebMCP tools and shared human/agent rules engine.
checkout_purchase pauses through requestUserInteraction and approval card explains the rule fired.
Frame sheet visibly shows agent orchestration alongside a shoe storefront, though not a confirmed purchase.
execution_rationale: The packet presents a coherent governance-centered storefront and visible shopping UI, but the frame evidence does not prove the full checkout, approval, ledger, and undo flow end to end.
execution_evidence: Live demo is reported alive and public repository exists.
Frame sheet shows storefront product grid/detail states and agent progress.
No video transcript and no clear proof of completed checkout.
impact_rationale: Agentic purchasing safety is a concrete problem for shoppers and the proposed limits, approvals, and audit trail address a specific trust gap.
impact_evidence: Pitch centers on consumer control over agent spending.
Described monthly, per-purchase, category, merchant, approval, receipt, and undo controls.
creativity_rationale: The product turns ambiguous agent checkout into an explicit governance interaction embedded in commerce rather than merely adding shopping automation.
creativity_evidence: Server-side policy engine plus human-in-the-loop checkout is a distinctive interaction model.
Hash-chained receipt ledger and five-minute escape hatch deepen the concept.
usability_note: The described approval card and visible rule explanations suggest good usability; full flow is not observed.
red_flags: Claims about standards and market research are not independently evidenced in packet.
Full purchase flow is not visible.
standouts: Human approval is a first-class product state, not a disclaimer.
Same rules engine for human and agent lanes.
advance_reason: Strong WebMCP-centered commerce governance concept with credible visible storefront evidence.

one_line: A shared marketplace canvas for people and outside agents.
what_it_does: A peer-to-peer marketplace and durable workspace where agents search, compare, research, organize boards, and draft deals while humans approve consequential actions.
leverage_rationale: The shared durable canvas and structured marketplace state are central: agents and humans work in one live workspace with focused tool packs, citations, approvals, and persistent decisions.
leverage_evidence: Transcript describes shared durable canvas, persistent core, and 121 structured tools.
Agent and human share listings, boards, research, notes, decisions, undo history, and trade rooms.
Frame sheet visibly shows marketplace/product and outdoor listing states.
execution_rationale: The packet is unusually coherent and ambitious, with a detailed workflow and video transcript covering browsing through trade approval; visual frames support marketplace states, though not every claimed feature is visible.
execution_evidence: 165-second video with detailed end-to-end transcript.
Demo reported alive and public repo exists.
Transcript covers listing search, research notebook, offer drafting, approvals, and shared state.
impact_rationale: Collectors and buyers of complex used goods have a real coordination and research problem, and a persistent agent-assisted workbench plausibly provides substantial value.
impact_evidence: Specific audience: people browsing cars, boats, campers, motorcycles, and machinery.
Addresses fragmented tabs, rigid alerts, scattered research, and difficult multi-party trades.
creativity_rationale: The concept is a memorable synthesis of marketplace, shared canvas, agent research notebook, and approval-boundary trade workflow without embedding an LLM in the product.
creativity_evidence: Outside agents are collaborators rather than a built-in chatbot.
Durable marketplace state, focused capability packs, cited research, and multi-party trade rooms are unusually deep.
usability_note: Canvas-first human workflow and explicit verification boundary are promising; login and broad scope add complexity.
red_flags: Very broad claimed scope relative to what can be visually verified from contact sheets.
standouts: Clear separation between fluid research and human-only consequential actions.
advance_reason: Top-tier WebMCP leverage and originality with unusually strong transcript-backed workflow evidence.

one_line: Deterministic Photoshop-like editing through an agent.
what_it_does: A Rust image-editing engine with segmentation and deterministic transformations exposed to an AI agent so users can watch and tweak true edits.
leverage_rationale: Structured image-editing operations and segmentation let an agent modify a live image precisely rather than regenerate it; WebMCP bridges an existing engine to external agents.
leverage_evidence: About text describes Rust engine, segmentation tool, and WebMCP bridge.
Frame montage shows dark editing workspace with blue-toned image and tool/interface states.
execution_rationale: The approach is technically plausible and the packet shows an editing workspace, but no video or public repository is supplied and the full edit result is not clearly demonstrated.
execution_evidence: Demo reported alive.
Frame sheets show image-editing UI states.
No transcript, public repo, or confirmed end-to-end edit evidence.
impact_rationale: Non-destructive, controllable editing addresses a real limitation of generative image editing for users who need fidelity and tweakability.
impact_evidence: Explicit problem framing around regeneration artifacts and loss of control.
Segmentation plus deterministic transformations target practical photo editing needs.
creativity_rationale: Combining agent interaction with deterministic pixel operations and object-level segmentation is a meaningful alternative to prompt-to-image regeneration.
creativity_evidence: True-edit framing and user-tweakable operations.
Custom Rust engine rather than only wrapping image generation.
usability_note: The watch-and-tweak model is user-friendly in principle, but interaction quality is not fully evidenced.
red_flags: Author says the custom engine and built-in tools predated the challenge.
No public repository and no transcript.
advance_reason: Strong concept and leverage, though execution evidence is thinner than leading packets.

one_line: A workout tracker sharing live session state with an agent.
what_it_does: A no-login workout tracker where agents adapt exercises, explain progression, and log only user-confirmed sets against the same live session data.
leverage_rationale: WebMCP places the agent in the live workout document, allowing reliable state-aware adaptation and exact logging rather than chat memory or separate sync.
leverage_evidence: About text explicitly contrasts shared page state with chat memory and API sync.
Agent can adapt remaining exercises while preserving completed sets and cite history/rules.
Devpost preview visibly shows a fitness interface.
execution_rationale: The central workout workflow is coherent and detailed, with live demo, public repo, and video submission; transcript is absent, so some behavior remains claimed.
execution_evidence: Demo alive, public AGPL repository, and 178-second video.
About text specifies adaptation, history-based progression, and confirmation before logging.
Frame evidence shows workout application states.
impact_rationale: Gym users have a concrete need for flexible, context-aware plans and reliable logging during short, changing sessions.
impact_evidence: Specific use case: adapting around pain, time, equipment, and completed work.
Agent explanations cite actual training history and progression rule.
creativity_rationale: The live-session shared-state framing is fresh and well matched to workouts, though the fitness tracker category is familiar.
creativity_evidence: Agent acts on the active workout rather than merely generating a plan.
User-confirmed logging avoids invented numbers.
usability_note: No-login flow and confirmation semantics are strong; gym-context details are not fully observable.
red_flags: No transcript and frame contact sheets are small.
Health-related adaptation warrants careful boundaries beyond the packet.
standouts: Concrete anti-hallucination behavior for logging sets.
advance_reason: Compelling practical WebMCP use with strong product and evidence coherence.

one_line: A queryable, versioned, accessible floor plan.
what_it_does: A floor-plan system whose validated route graph answers accessibility questions, checks clearance, and supports human-approved venue corrections.
leverage_rationale: The key answers are computed from structured building topology and body constraints but are not rendered in the UI; WebMCP exposes capabilities a general UI-driving agent could not reliably discover.
leverage_evidence: Transcript demonstrates route, clearance, blocking-door explanation, versioning, and approved/declined reports.
About text says answers are computed from geometry and absent from the DOM.
Fourteen tools expose route and venue state.
execution_rationale: The transcript gives unusually strong end-to-end evidence across successful routes, blocked routes, approvals, version refresh, and declined reports; frame sheet visibly supports floor-plan UI.
execution_evidence: 178-second video with detailed end-to-end transcript.
Demo alive and public repository exists.
Transcript covers 13/13 style state progression and immutable declined report.
impact_rationale: Disabled and low-vision visitors have a high-stakes, specific need for reliable indoor accessibility answers before and during a visit.
impact_evidence: Specific wheelchair-width clearance scenario and step-free routing.
Tool returns reasons and blocking doorway rather than opaque failure.
Venue correction workflow reduces stale plan risk.
creativity_rationale: Turning a static floor plan into an agent-queryable, versioned accessibility authority with explainable topology updates is highly original and deeply pursued.
creativity_evidence: Computed answers are not simple page actions.
Approval/decline audit semantics and route graph versioning are integrated into the interaction model.
usability_note: Natural questions, explicit uncertainty, and explanations of barriers are excellent usability choices.
red_flags: Core floor-plan parser existed before challenge according to about text.
standouts: WebMCP exposes non-rendered computed knowledge with auditably approved updates.
advance_reason: Exceptional leverage, impact, creativity, and unusually complete workflow evidence.

one_line: A browser spreadsheet whose calculation engine is agent-operable.
what_it_does: A local browser spreadsheet exposing range reads/writes, formulas, formatting, structure, undo, focus, and recalculation results to an agent.
leverage_rationale: WebMCP gives an external agent precise access to live workbook state and dependency recalculation, with intermediate changed-cell results and shared focus; UI automation is substantially less reliable.
leverage_evidence: About text explains IronCalc WASM holds the live workbook in memory with no remote copy.
Writes return recalculation ripple and agent/user edits share the document.
Frame sheet visibly shows spreadsheet/table states.
execution_rationale: The architecture and interaction contract are coherent, and spreadsheet UI evidence is visible, but there is no video or transcript to prove the central agent-edit loop end to end.
execution_evidence: Demo alive and public repository exists.
Description specifies twelve tools and detailed write/recalculation behavior.
Devpost preview visibly shows populated spreadsheet UI.
impact_rationale: Model builders and spreadsheet users benefit from reliable formula-aware collaboration without copying data into a separate interpreter.
impact_evidence: Specific problem: stable cell addresses, dependency graph, editable intermediate values.
Shared human/agent editing and attached user changes address real workflow friction.
creativity_rationale: The product treats the spreadsheet engine and its dependency graph as the agent's execution substrate, not merely a canvas controlled by clicks.
creativity_evidence: Recalculation ripple is part of the tool contract.
Agent focus color and edit attachment create a distinct collaborative interaction.
usability_note: Stable addresses and editable results are strong; dense spreadsheet workflows remain inherently complex.
red_flags: No video/transcript; several advanced behaviors are only described.
standouts: Clear explanation of why live local workbook state matters.
advance_reason: Strong, technically specific WebMCP leverage with a credible spreadsheet use case.

one_line: A personal portfolio augmented with WebMCP navigation tools.
what_it_does: A minimal portfolio linked to Substack that adds tools for agents to navigate the site and inspect linked work.
leverage_rationale: The packet describes agent navigation and tool listing, but a general browser agent can achieve the same outcome trivially through ordinary links and UI actions.
leverage_evidence: About text says the pre-existing portfolio was aligned with WebMCP.
Claims demo shows navigation and tool execution via DevTools, but no frame sheets were submitted.
execution_rationale: The portfolio likely exists, but evidence is thin and the description is mostly self-report with no video or frame sheets proving a complete agent workflow.
execution_evidence: Public repo and live demo are reported.
One gallery image only; no submitted video frames.
About text is sparse and includes a generated architecture diagram rather than product proof.
impact_rationale: A personal portfolio has a legitimate audience, but the agent capability offers limited additional value and the packet does not identify a meaningful user problem beyond discovery.
impact_evidence: Stated purpose is personal work experience and Substack listing.
No specific agent-centered audience or consequential workflow described.
creativity_rationale: Adding standard WebMCP navigation tools to an existing portfolio is a derivative application with little novel interaction model.
creativity_evidence: Author explicitly says the website predated the challenge.
Implementation is described as asking Gemini to align existing HTML/CSS/JS with WebMCP.
usability_note: A minimal portfolio may be easy to browse, but agent utility is not demonstrated.
red_flags: Evidence relies heavily on a Devpost narrative and a claimed DevTools demo.
advance_reason: WebMCP appears cosmetic and the packet lacks sufficient product evidence.

one_line: Agent-assisted business email and DNS setup with human send control.
what_it_does: A Shipmail interface exposing inbox, domain, DNS, propagation, and mailbox setup tools while keeping send/delete/forward and credentials out of agent control.
leverage_rationale: Structured page-specific email and DNS tools reduce setup copying and preserve permissions, but much of the workflow could be performed by a general browser agent with real friction.
leverage_evidence: About text describes page-contextual tools, authentication, permissions, pause/resume registration, and receipts.
Frame montage includes email/setup interface states.
Human presses Send and irreversible actions are excluded.
execution_rationale: The scope is coherent and safety boundaries are clearly designed, with live demo, public repo, and multiple gallery images, but no video or transcript demonstrates the complete setup flow.
execution_evidence: Demo alive, public repo, and three gallery images.
Description specifies inbox, domains, DNS records, mailbox creation, pause/resume.
Frames show email-like and form/setup states.
impact_rationale: Small businesses and domain owners face tedious, error-prone email/DNS setup; exact records and propagation checks offer credible value.
impact_evidence: Specific setup workflow across Shipmail and DNS.
Agent removes copying/checklist burden while retaining human send control.
creativity_rationale: Permission-aware browser agents for email setup are a useful synthesis, though the category and individual actions are familiar.
creativity_evidence: Pause removes signed-in tools and resume creates a new controller.
Explicit exclusion of send/delete/forward and credentials is thoughtfully integrated.
usability_note: Receipts, pause/resume, exact DNS output, and human send boundary are clear usability/safety choices.
red_flags: No video or transcript; gallery/frame evidence is limited.
advance_reason: Practical, safety-conscious agent workflow with meaningful though not transformative WebMCP delta.

one_line: A local-first word-association game for humans and multiple agents.
what_it_does: A shared synchronized game where agents receive rules and role-scoped state through WebMCP and take validated turns alongside people.
leverage_rationale: WebMCP is part of the game loop: it supplies authoritative rules, identity, private state, and legal actions to multiple agents sharing one match rather than bolting on a chatbot.
leverage_evidence: About text specifies context, identity, read, and validated write tools.
Independent tabs synchronize through same-origin storage/events/polling.
Frame evidence is absent and Devpost preview is blocked by a security-verification message.
execution_rationale: The described game architecture is coherent, but no frame sheets or usable video evidence show the board, agent turns, or complete match flow, so execution is capped.
execution_evidence: Public repo and live demo are reported.
Detailed description covers lobby, role-scoped state, turns, and synchronization.
Devpost screenshot visibly shows connection/security verification failure rather than gameplay.
impact_rationale: Cooperative and competitive word play has a clear audience, and removing bot setup friction could make agent participation accessible to nontechnical players.
impact_evidence: Specific game audience and social play model.
No model picker, API key, or prompt setup required according to description.
creativity_rationale: Making agent roles, private information, and synchronized turns part of a word game is a fresh interaction model, especially with page-delivered rules.
creativity_evidence: Agents are players with roles rather than assistants.
get_rules skill/context distribution and multi-tab participation are inventive.
usability_note: No-setup invitation is promising, but gameplay usability cannot be visually checked.
red_flags: Devpost embedded content visibly fails security verification; core gameplay is unverified.
standouts: Authoritative page-delivered rules and role-scoped state.
advance_reason: Creative and promising, but the complete lack of inspectable gameplay evidence prevents advancing at this stage.

what_it_does: A synchronized car configurator and digital twin with an owner guide and 3D creation tools exposed through 49 WebMCP registrations.
leverage_rationale: Structured tools operate across configuration, a shared 3D garage, measured components, guide queries, and creation workflow; this is more precise than generic UI driving, though breadth risks making WebMCP a large action surface.
leverage_evidence: About text enumerates 49 tools across five page contexts.
Claims revision-gated undoable mutations, shared 3D vehicle, measurements, and source-basis results.
Frame sheets visibly show AutoLab promotional/configuration and vehicle listing states.
execution_rationale: The packet presents a coherent multi-surface product and visual frames show automotive/configuration content, but no video/transcript demonstrates the claimed cross-context workflow end to end.
execution_evidence: Demo alive and public repo exists.
Frame sheets show AutoLab and vehicle catalog/configuration screens.
Description specifies React/Three.js/Vitest/Playwright implementation and multiple page contexts.
impact_rationale: Car buyers and owners can benefit from understandable configuration, ownership outcomes, component inspection, and a persistent digital twin, though the fictional-car scope limits immediate practical reach.
impact_evidence: Specific tasks include pricing, ownership outcomes, measurements, and owner-guide queries.
Human interruption and revision-gated mutations address consequential configuration changes.
creativity_rationale: The combination of vehicle configurator, measured 3D digital twin, owner guide, and code-native creation engine is ambitious and memorable.
creativity_evidence: Five connected contexts and 49 tools pursue an agent-operable vehicle lifecycle.
Independent reconstruction explicitly distinguishes itself from manufacturer CAD.
usability_note: Shared 3D controls and undo/approval semantics are promising, but the broad surface may be complex.
red_flags: No video/transcript; many claims rely on description.
Fictional vehicle and marketing-like frame variants limit direct real-world validation.
standouts: Measurement and source-basis claims show care for grounded results.
